authoredSolutions.3: With constant power, \(Fv = P\), so \(mv\frac{dv}{dt} = P\). Starting from rest, \(\int_{0}^{v} v\,dv = \frac{P}{m}\int_{0}^{t} dt\) gives \(v = \sqrt{\frac{2P}{m}}\,t^{1/2}\). Then \(\frac{dx}{dt} = \sqrt{\frac{2P}{m}}\,t^{1/2}\), and with \(x = 0\) at \(t = 0\), \[x = \sqrt{\frac{2P}{m}}\cdot\frac{2}{3}\,t^{3/2} \propto t^{3/2}.\] Hence option (b).
authoredSolutions.6: Both stars turn about their centre of mass with the same angular speed \(\omega\), separated by \(r_{1} + r_{2}\). For star 1: \(\frac{Gm_{1}m_{2}}{\left(r_{1} + r_{2}\right)^{2}} = m_{1}\omega^{2}r_{1}\). The centre of mass gives \(m_{1}r_{1} = m_{2}r_{2}\), so \(r_{1} = \frac{m_{2}\left(r_{1} + r_{2}\right)}{m_{1} + m_{2}}\). Substituting, \[\omega^{2} = \frac{G\left(m_{1} + m_{2}\right)}{\left(r_{1} + r_{2}\right)^{3}},\qquad T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = \frac{2\pi\left(r_{1} + r_{2}\right)^{3/2}}{\sqrt{G\left(m_{1} + m_{2}\right)}}.\] Option (c). As printed, option (a) \(2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\left(r_{1} + r_{2}\right)^{3}}{G\left(m_{1} + m_{2}\right)}}\) is the same expression, so (a) is equally correct; the key follows the booklet.
authoredSolutions.10: Let the path length be \(L\). Walking on the stationary escalator takes \(t_{1}\), so the boy's walking speed is \(\frac{L}{t_{1}}\). Standing on the moving escalator takes \(t_{2}\), so the escalator's speed is \(\frac{L}{t_{2}}\). Walking on the moving escalator, the speeds add: \[v = L\left(\frac{1}{t_{1}} + \frac{1}{t_{2}}\right).\] The time is \(\frac{L}{v} = \frac{t_{1}t_{2}}{t_{1} + t_{2}}\), option (d).
authoredSolutions.18: Apparent angle of dip in a vertical plane at angle \(\alpha\) to the magnetic meridian obeys \(\tan\delta' = \frac{\tan\delta}{\cos\alpha}\), where \(\delta\) is the true dip. Here \(\alpha = 30^{\circ}\) and \(\delta' = 45^{\circ}\), so \[\tan 45^{\circ} = \frac{\tan\delta}{\cos 30^{\circ}} \Rightarrow \tan\delta = \cos 30^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\] Hence the true dip is \(\delta = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right).\)
authoredSolutions.21: Count the \(\sigma\) bonds and lone pairs on nitrogen (the steric number). \(NO_{2}^{-}\): two \(\sigma\) bonds and one lone pair, steric number 3, \(sp^{2}\), bent. \(NO_{2}^{+}\): \(O=N^{+}=O\) has two \(\sigma\) bonds and no lone pair (it is isoelectronic with \(CO_{2}\)), steric number 2, \(sp\), linear. \(NH_{4}^{+}\): four \(\sigma\) bonds and no lone pair, steric number 4, \(sp^{3}\), tetrahedral. So the order is \(sp^{2}, sp, sp^{3}\), option (A).

\(4s^{2}4p^{1}\) is gallium: period 4, group 13. The diagonal neighbour one period down is one group to the right, i.e. period 5, group 14, which is tin (\(\mathrm{Sn}\), \(5s^{2}5p^{2}\)).

authoredSolutions.27: Rate of hydrolysis of acid derivatives follows the ease of departure of the leaving group (the more stable the leaving group, the faster the nucleophilic acyl substitution). authoredSolutions.35: The substrate is 3-bromobenzamide, \(m\text{-}Br\text{-}C_6H_4\text{-}CONH_2\). authoredSolutions.37: The intended route has three steps. First, benzoic anhydride benzoylates the ring (Friedel-Crafts acylation). The allyl group directs ortho and para, and the para position already carries Br, so the benzoyl group goes ortho to the allyl group. Second, HBr adds to the side-chain double bond by Markovnikov's rule. The first cation, \(Ar-CH_{2}-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_{3}\), is secondary; a 1,2-hydride shift moves the charge next to the ring and gives the more stable benzylic cation \(Ar-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_{2}-CH_{3}\), which takes up \(Br^{-}\). Third, fluoride replaces the bromine (a Swarts-type halogen exchange), so F ends up on the benzylic carbon. This is option (D). As printed the question is flawed: no Lewis acid (such as \(AlCl_{3}\)) is given for the acylation, and \(CaF_{2}\) is not a usual reagent for halogen exchange (the Swarts reaction uses \(AgF\), \(Hg_{2}F_{2}\), \(CoF_{2}\) or \(SbF_{3}\)). The key (D) follows the intended route.
authoredSolutions.38: The substrate carries three carbonyls: a ring ketone, an aldehyde \(-CHO\) and a terminal methyl ketone on the side chain. The result is a spiro diketone-derived compound with one cyclohexanone ring and one cyclohexenone ring, i.e. option (B).
